A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AnyAttack, and their main text, equations, tables, and figures are readable. v1 includes Appendix A, but the supplied v2 ends at the references despite repeatedly referring to an appendix. This limits comparison of supplementary results and implementation details.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval, classification, captioning, ablation, efficiency, and commercial-model experiments, including additional results in Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark and ablation results and adds quantitative Gemini/GPT evaluation in Table 4.

M1.justification: The frozen CLIP encoder, noise decoder, K-augmentation, temperature schedule, and auxiliary-model fine-tuning with cosine or bidirectional contrastive loss remain unchanged. Renaming LCon to LPre and emphasizing pre-training/fine-tuning do not introduce a new procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds prompted image-text relevance evaluation on commercial VLMs using MSCOCO targets, extending the earlier commercial image-description scenario. The named training and downstream datasets remain unchanged; later Flickr30K results are unavailable in the missing appendix.

E2.justification: Matched main experiments retain AttackVLM-ii/-it, SASD-WS-Cos/-MSE, and SU-Cos/-MSE. The new commercial benchmark reuses these same baseline variants rather than introducing additional comparison methods.

E3.justification: Section 4.5 adds a 100-image MSCOCO evaluation using an image-text relationship prompt and response options, with ASR defined by responses labeled relevant. GPT is added as a target model. The existing 1,000-image benchmark settings, perturbation budget, and reported training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 3 adds a GPT response to the existing cow-target commercial case study. The initialization, auxiliary-model, and loss ablations and efficiency analysis in Figures 4–5 remain unchanged. Further case-study changes cannot be checked because v2's referenced appendix is unavailable.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Tables and plots continue to present point estimates without uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v1 Tables 2–4 and v2 Tables 1–3 have unchanged numerical results. New v2 Table 4 reports AnyAttack ASRs of 31% on Gemini and 38% on GPT, versus 5% and 28% for the strongest baseline, SASD-WS-Cos. These are additional results under a new protocol; later Flickr30K values cannot be checked.

T1.justification: v2 omits the explicit target-label and target-image optimization formulations presented in v1 Table 1. The AnyAttack formulation moves to Equation 1, while its contrastive losses and temperature equation remain mathematically unchanged. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: v2 replaces the highlighted contrastive-loss contribution with a claim of first adopting large-scale pre-training and fine-tuning for targeted attacks, and describes the generator as a foundation model. Commercial transfer claims expand from three models to four through GPT; the central self-supervised attack claim remains.

C2.justification: v2 removes the specific explanations linking limited random-image pools to overfitting and auxiliary-model diversity to complementarity. It adds the smaller downstream dataset as the reason for using external random images during fine-tuning. Interpretations of the retained ablations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 newly states that model weights are released and retains the principal training and hardware details. However, its referenced appendix is unavailable, preventing comparison with v1's exact VLM configurations, library and repository instructions, and additional prompting details. The full extent of the reproducibility changes is unresolved.

R1.justification: References to Chen et al. (2020), He et al. (2020), and Liu et al. (2017) disappear. Positioning shifts toward the first large-scale pre-training/fine-tuning paradigm, while the related-work discussion and identification of AttackVLM as the closest work largely remain.

P1.justification: The title and selected abstract, introduction, and method passages are rewritten, with revised terminology and separate quantitative/qualitative commercial-results paragraphs. The main section order remains stable. v2 introduces incorrect section references where Sections 4.3–4.5 should refer to result tables.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column layout, redraws Figures 1–3, moves the introductory diagram onto the first page, and reformats result tables with horizontal model labels. It adds the commercial-results table and relocates/resizes the retained ablation and efficiency plots, substantially changing the visual organization.

improvement.justification: The new 100-image commercial comparison adds quantitative evidence beyond v1's selected examples, and redesigned diagrams clarify the unchanged framework. However, v2's promised appendix is missing, leaving supplementary evidence and implementation details unavailable, while incorrect cross-references hinder verification. These competing changes prevent a reliable judgment of net overall quality.
